Advantages: 100% objective, instantly automated, standard across benchmarks.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Tests test-taking memory, not clinical reasoning or conversational safety.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Absolute string identity for clinical entity extraction.
Advantages: Strict and binary; ideal for ICD-10 codes, lab values, and drug names.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Overly rigid; penalizes valid synonyms, casing differences, or rephrasing.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Exact word n-gram precision against target doctor notes.
Advantages: Fast, low-cost baseline for multi-word generation tasks.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Ignores medical synonyms; penalizes valid medical phrasing; misses context.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) recall in clinical summaries.
Advantages: Captures text structure, order, and sentence-level content retention well.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Swapping or negating a single word alters clinical meaning completely without dropping score.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Deep semantic token-level similarity using vector embeddings.
Advantages: Recognizes clinical paraphrasing, synonyms, and semantic equivalence.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: High scores can still occur on fluent, highly polished, but completely false assertions.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Percentage of flagged AI errors that are genuine hallucinations.
Advantages: Minimizes false alarms when deploying automated verification tools.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Ignores unflagged hallucinations that slip through unnoticed.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Percentage of total actual hallucinations successfully detected.
Advantages: Crucial for safety; measures the pipeline's ability to catch dangerous errors.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: High recall can lead to excessive false alarms if the verifier is oversensitive.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Harmonic mean balancing detection precision and recall.
Advantages: Optimal single metric for evaluating imbalanced error detection tasks.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Obscures specific trade-offs between precision and recall in a single value.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Ability of the model to refrain from answering when uncertain.
Advantages: Dramatically reduces overconfident false advice and hallucination rates.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Excessive abstention degrades model utility and user satisfaction.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Verification of advice against official medical practice guidelines.
Advantages: Directly measures clinical truth and adherence to evidence-based practice.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Subject to inter-physician disagreement; slow and expensive to evaluate.

Formula / Scoring Logic: Likert Scale (0 = No Harm to 3 = Severe)
Primary Evaluation Focus: Severity and likelihood of patient injury if AI advice is followed.
Advantages: Gold-standard metric for clinical safety and risk mitigation.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Non-automated; requires panels of licensed, board-certified medical experts.

Primary Evaluation Focus: Blind side-by-side preference comparison (AI vs. Human Doctor).
Advantages: Evaluates real-world clinical usability, tone, completeness, and reasoning.
Limitations / Clinical Risks: Highly resource-intensive; difficult to integrate into automated CI/CD pipelines.
